trends.name: Coding agents enter the large-scale repository operations stage
trends.summary: OpenAI showed iFood scaling coding agents across 15,000 code repositories, while the open-source community released team management and pluggable execution tools.
trends.attention_driver: As the number of repositories and tasks covered by agents rises, teams need unified task assignment, permissions and quality control.

evidence.quote: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
evidence.claim: Supports that coding agents have organizational deployment cases across large numbers of code repositories.

evidence.quote: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
evidence.claim: Supports that the developer community sees changes in agent capabilities as an important recent inflection point.

evidence.quote: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work
evidence.claim: Supports that demand is forming for tools to manage agents in work settings.

trends.so_what: The bottleneck for coding agent products will lie in multi-repository context, change review and accountability tracking, rather than single-generation performance. Prioritize observable task queues and tiered execution permissions to avoid leaving scaling costs to engineering teams.

trends.name: Agent cost pressure drives model compression and inference optimization
trends.summary: Cost issues for multi-agent long contexts have appeared in the same cycle as model compression and faster prefill optimization.
trends.attention_driver: As task chains grow longer, repeated context reading and high-concurrency serving quickly raise the cost per task.

evidence.quote: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive.
evidence.claim: Supports that multi-agent workflows driven by frontier models face clear cost pressure.

evidence.quote: shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB
evidence.claim: Supports that model compression methods for low-storage deployment are being used for agent coding models.
Supports that the serving community is focusing on prefill speed and inference kernel optimization.

trends.so_what: Agent pricing cannot be estimated only by call volume. Context reuse, model routing and prefill latency directly determine gross margin and interaction limits. Product teams should measure the cost of each successful completion on real task chains, rather than compare only single-turn prices.

trends.name: Sensitive enterprise tasks drive private inference commitments
trends.summary: Reports say OpenAI is testing Private Inference, claiming enterprises can use powerful models without letting the service provider view query data.
trends.attention_driver: The usable boundary for sensitive data still limits enterprises from using agents in core processes.

evidence.quote: OpenAI is testing a new feature called "Private Inference"
evidence.claim: Supports that OpenAI is testing private inference features for sensitive enterprise tasks.

evidence.quote: GPT-6.1 Sol is available starting today to all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users
evidence.claim: Supports that OpenAI continues to expand access to high-capability models for organizational accounts.

trends.so_what: Enterprise differentiation will be determined more by data isolation, audit evidence and key control, rather than model rankings alone. Product roadmaps should first identify which workloads must be verifiably isolated, then match retrieval, logging and operations design.

watch_list.name: Meta Muse seeks e-commerce entry points and integrates with Instagram DMs
watch_list.summary: Meta Muse has entered Walmart shopping scenarios, and reports say Amazon is discussing lifting its access restrictions.
watch_list.attention_driver: Whether shopping agents can obtain platform entry points, complete transactions and retain attribution has become a focus of product competition.

evidence.quote: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
evidence.claim: Supports that Muse has gained access to retail shopping scenarios.

evidence.quote: Amazon and Meta are in talks to bring back Muse
evidence.claim: Supports that Amazon and Meta are discussing market access arrangements for Muse.

evidence.quote: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
evidence.claim: Supports that Muse is expanding distribution through Meta-owned user touchpoints.

watch_list.so_what: Transaction-facing agents do not depend only on conversational ability. Entry permissions, merchant data and settlement responsibility determine deliverable features. If your product involves acting on behalf of users or making purchases, make authorization, failure fallback and attribution primary experiences.

insights.text: Agent operations become a product layer: as multi-agent coverage expands, permissions, task assignment and review will outweigh the single-generation experience
Costs need to be measured per successful task: context and prefill costs in long task chains will limit agent pricing and interaction depth
Agent tools continue to multiply: frameworks, terminal agents and MCP tools are launching in the same period, and integration burden will keep rising
